'''Dauch Corporation''', formerly '''American Axle & Manufacturing, Inc.''' ('''AAM'''),<ref name="rename"/> headquartered in [[Detroit, Michigan]], is an American manufacturer of [[automobile]] driveline and drivetrain components and systems.

== History ==
American Axle & Manufacturing (AAM) was founded in 1994 when a private investor group, led by [[Richard E Dauch|Richard E. "Dick" Dauch]], James W. McLernon, Raymond Park and Morton E. Harris purchased the Final Drive and Forge Business Unit from GM's Saginaw Division.

In 1999, AAM went public, and was traded as "AXL" on the [[New York Stock Exchange]] (NYSE) until becoming "DCH" on its 2026 renaming to Dauch.<ref name="rename"/> AAM grew to supply various OEM manufacturers around the globe in the passenger car, light truck, and commercial vehicle segments.

The company's World Headquarters building, erected in 2004, is located on the [[Detroit]]/[[Hamtramck]] border.

AAM was renamed Dauch in 2026.<ref name="rename">{{cite press release |url=https://www.aam.com/media/story/american-axle---manufacturing-holdings--inc.-to-become--dauch-corporation--and-trade-on-nyse-under-new-ticker-symbol--dch |title=American Axle & Manufacturing Holdings, Inc. to Become “Dauch Corporation” and Trade on NYSE Under New Ticker Symbol “DCH” |date=26 January 2026 |publisher=Dauch |accessdate=19 March 2026}}</ref>

== 2008 strike ==
On February 26, 2008, approximately 4600 AAM employees went on what would be a three-month-long strike to protest a proposed wage and benefit cut by the company's management. The proposal would reduce production workers' hourly wage from $28 to $18 and cut skilled trade wages $5 per hour.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://anti-union.blogspot.com/2008/03/american-axle-strike.html|title=Joe's Union Review: American Axle strike|date=2008-03-02|website=Joe's Union Review|access-date=2019-10-09}}</ref> The strike cost [[General Motors]] $2.6 billion as the automaker lost the production of its [[Chevrolet Malibu]] sedan and other vehicles.<ref name="AT-GM Slash">[http://www.autotrends.org/gm-to-slash-expenses-raise-cash-to-move-forward/ "GM To Slash Expenses, Raise Cash To Move Forward"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719235118/http://www.autotrends.org/gm-to-slash-expenses-raise-cash-to-move-forward/ |date=2008-07-19 }}. Auto Trends. Retrieved 18 July 2008.</ref>

== 2026 strike ==
On midnight at June 1, 2026, the [[United Auto Workers]] declared a strike at Dauch's [[Three Rivers, Michigan | Three Rivers]] production facility, affecting nearly 1,000 employees, in response to Dauch failing to reach a deal with the union regarding wage hikes before the May 31 deadline. UAW president [[Shawn Fain]] criticized the company for making an "empire of profit" of $8.4 billion since the UAW agreed to drop wages in 2008. In response to the strike, the company stated it "believes that the best outcomes for everyone – our Associates, the union, and the Company – are reached at the bargaining table.  We remain committed to negotiating with the union in good faith and hope to promptly reach a fair agreement."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rappleye |first1=Liam Rappleye |title=UAW declares midnight strike at American Axle, a key GM supplier |url=https://www.freep.com/story/money/cars/2026/05/31/uaw-members-to-strike-at-american-axle-no-contract-no-axles/90347993007/ |access-date=1 June 2026 |work=Detroit Free Press |agency=Detroit Free Press}}</ref>

==Products==
Key products include [[axle]]s, [[drive shaft]]s, [[front axle]], [[universal joint]]s and sealing and thermal-management products.

== Demolition ==
After closing its factories in Detroit in 2012, American Axle and Manufacturing had started a demolition project. In late 2013, much of the old manufacturing facility had been demolished by bulldozers and cranes. Also, in February 2014, it was reported and confirmed that most of the Detroit/Hamtramck manufacturing site had been sold <ref name="Detroit News">[https://anti-union.blogspot.com/2008/03/american-axle-strike.html "American Axle sells Detroit manufacturing complex to Industrial Realty Group"], The Detroit News. Burden Melissa. Retrieved 24 February 2014.</ref> to a California-based Industrial Realty Group, IRG LLC who specialize in the use of industrial buildings for other developments such as apartment complexes. In 2014, American Axle continued to own its headquarters and greenbelt property at the site. It planned to build an engineering facility in the sole building left standing from the original manufacturing complex.

==UK subsidiary==
{{main|Albion Motors}}
Albion Automotive is a [[Glasgow]]-based subsidiary.<ref>Just Auto, [https://www.just-auto.com/news/albion-secures-axle-contract-with-renault-trucks_id83103.aspx UK: Albion secures axle contract with Renault Trucks], published 5 August 2002, accessed 8 November 2020</ref>

In 2002, the [[Court of Appeal (England and Wales)|Court of Appeal]] ruled in a case brought by staff employed at Albion's [[Farington]] site in [[Lancashire]], ''Albion Automotive Ltd w. Walker and others'',<ref>England and Wales Court of Appeal (Civil Division), [https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2002/946.html Albion Automotive Ltd v Walker & Ors], EWCA Civil 946 (21 June 2002), accessed 8 March 2021</ref> that a contractual term entitling employees to an enhanced [[redundancy payment]] could be implied into the employees' [[contract of employment|contracts of employment]] based on the employer's custom and practice.<ref>Consilio, [https://web.archive.org/web/20061117142221/http://www.spr-consilio.com/artemploy4.htm Enhanced Redundancy Payments], published 16 December 2002, archived version accessed 8 November 2020</ref>
